text.p: A Catholic anti-abortion group strongly appealed to the Mexican government on Friday to stop forced sterilisation and said thousands of poor Indian women had been subjected to the practice.

"Women are being trampled. Their rights are being trampled," Pro-Vida director Jorge Serrano Limon told a news conference. "Sterilizing our population against its will is a complete violation of human rights," he said.
"We want to make an anguished appeal to the president to stop this genocide. We can't let it happen that after these campaigns we are going to have a sterile Mexico."

Serrano said Pro-Vida had documented more than 300 cases of forced sterilisation in government medical facilities over the past three years and knew of "several thousand" others where women had refused to come forward publicly. Most of the sterilisations were in poor Indian or rural areas, in particular in the states of Oaxaca, Puebla and Chiapas.

A Health Ministry spokesman denied the government had any campaign to sterilise Mexicans forcibly. The official strategy was to "inform the population about all contraceptive methods so the population can take an informed decision" he said.

The Pro-Vida group presented to reporters a young woman from Puebla state who told of her experiences when she entered the Huejotzingo hospital, 50 miles (80 km) east of Mexico City, to give birth in February.

"As the doctor put on his mask and cap and prepared his gloves he said 'We are going to tie your tubes,'" said the woman, Rocio Garrido. "I was already lying down and they had already anaesthetised me. When I asked why, he said 'Because we are, my dear. All the women who come here get one (treatment) or another -- it's part of a campaign,'" she said.

Garrido, 22, said she found out after leaving the hospital that the doctor had planted an IUD (intra-uterine contraceptive device) in her without telling her. The group showed a copy of the hospital records to back up its claim.

More than 40 women from another part of Puebla sued the Mexican state health institute IMSS this year for allegedly planting IUDs in them without their consent or knowledge and infecting their wombs through unsanitary procedures when they went for a routine checkup. A decision is pending in the case.

Pro-Vida regards IUDs as a form of sterilisation because the devices, which the anti-abortion group says are often implanted without the knowledge of the woman, make it virtually impossible to become pregnant.
